src/infrastructure/http/project-controller.ts and src/infrastructure/http/user-controller.ts: create() uses requiredString(req.body, "name") instead of checking the body inline.
src/infrastructure/http/task-controller.ts: add/list/assign use requiredString, optionalString and queryString the same way.
src/infrastructure/http/error-middleware.ts: STATUS_BY_KIND (Record<ApplicationErrorKind, number>) is the only mapping from error kind to HTTP status, and no controller sets error statuses itself.
ProjectController, TaskController and UserController all inject use cases through the constructor and expose routes(): Router.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module has one job: it is the HTTP adapter that turns Express requests into use-case calls and application errors into HTTP responses. Each rule is defined once. Body and query parsing and validation live only in request-fields.ts, and every controller uses those helpers instead of reading req.body directly. The mapping from error kind to HTTP status lives only in error-middleware.ts. The controllers throw ApplicationError (through the helpers) and never set error statuses themselves. All three controllers share the same shape: the constructor receives use cases, routes() returns an Express Router, and private handlers do the work. Path parameters are read with String(req.params[...]) in several places. This is a small repeated idiom, not a duplicated invariant. The `?? ""` default for description in TaskController.add is a request-level default and does not conflict with anything visible here. I found no unrelated concerns, duplicated invariants or bypassed abstractions.
